name: BACH_0078
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (100%)** · Confident · Careful review

The 90% set holds Invasive only, and the second model agrees [F1]. The case is flagged tier 2 because Invasive is the top class.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 100%, InSitu <1% | One dominant class |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.996; 64th percentile | Typical, usable input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model agrees |
| Similar cases | 5/5 Invasive | Neighbors all match |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 3, 8) · ↑ invasive · Above-typical score; concept model links it to invasion [F2] · Validated
- **Variation in nuclear size** (regions 0, 4, 11) · context · Highest in reference set; mean nuclear area lowest [F8] · Measured
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 4, 9, 10) · ↑ invasive · Scored high, but AI spot check 3/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47 to 0.60). The heatmap is faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: The deletion effect (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so concepts are not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis (3/20) and mitoses (0/20) are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Calibration was tested on 132 images; ECE upper bound is 0.18, so 100% may be overconfident.
- Smallest mean nuclear area in reference set is unusual; cells were measured in only regions 0, 4, 11.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 3, 8**: Confirm stromal invasion where the infiltrating-stroma score is highest.
2. **Regions 4, 9, 10**: Verify whether necrosis is truly present; its spot check was poor.
3. **Regions 2, 7**: Lowest per-region invasive probability (36%); check whether these are non-invasive tissue.
